(01)
THE BRIEF
From reactive fixes to a visible rhythm of care and improvement.
A mock support experience that makes requests, priorities, fixes, and follow-up easier to understand.
THE CHALLENGE
Requests arrived by email, phone and hallway conversation. Urgent problems waited behind small ones, the same issues came back every few weeks, and nobody could see what had already been tried.
THE GOAL
Give the team one place to ask for help, priorities everyone agrees on, and fixes that stay fixed.
OUR ROLE
Support audit, intake and triage design, root-cause fixes, knowledge base, and a monthly care rhythm.
HEADLINE RESULT
26h → 1.5h
first response time
Sample figure
CLIENT
Operations team, 40 people
SECTOR
Business operations
TIMELINE
6 weeks + monthly care
TEAM
Support, systems and documentation
STATUS
Mock project
(02)
HOW WE GOT THERE
SERVICE LOG
Every step,
logged like a ticket.
We treated the support set-up itself as a series of tickets: each one opened with a problem and closed with a change.
Support set-up log
5 tickets
SUP-01
Week 1
Audit the requests
Reviewed three months of requests and grouped 214 tickets by cause. Four root causes created more than half of the volume.
214 requests reviewed
4 root causes
Closed
SUP-02
Week 2
One way to ask
Replaced scattered emails with one request form that captures device, urgency and screenshots up front.
Request form
Shared inbox retired
Closed
SUP-03
Week 3
Agree priorities
Set four priority levels with response targets, so urgent problems move first and everyone knows what to expect.
Priority levels
Response targets
Closed
SUP-04
Weeks 4–5
Fix and document
Fixed the four root causes and wrote a short knowledge-base article for each, so the next person solves it in minutes.
4 root-cause fixes
12 help articles
Closed
SUP-05
Monthly
Review and improve
A monthly care report shows volume, response times and what we improved, before small issues become big ones.
Care report
Improvement backlog
Ongoing
(03)
WHAT WE DELIVERED
Clear priorities,
clear promises.
The priority model agreed with the team. Every request is sorted on arrival, and every level has a response target.
P1
Critical
The business has stopped
RESPONSE TARGET
30 min
P2

A team is blocked
RESPONSE TARGET

P3

A workaround exists
RESPONSE TARGET

P4
Planned
An improvement request
RESPONSE TARGET
Next care cycle

THE RESULTS
Before and after,
side by side.
Support results compare the three months before the change with the three months after, using the same request log.
